claims: The Artemis II mission is a 10-day crewed lunar flyby.
The Artemis II mission launched on April 1, 2026.
The Artemis II mission uses the SLS rocket.
The Artemis II mission includes a 24-hour initial Earth orbit for system checks.
The crew will perform a translunar injection to enter a "figure-eight" path around the Moon.
The Artemis II mission reaches the lunar vicinity around day 5-6.
Artemis II launches from Kennedy Space Center Complex 39B at 6:35 p.m. ET on April 1, 2026.
On Day 1 of Artemis II, Orion separates from the ICPS upper stage.
On Day 1 of Artemis II, Orion deploys solar arrays.
On Day 1 of Artemis II, Orion performs a 90-minute initial orbit followed by a 24-hour high Earth orbit check.
On Days 2-4 of Artemis II, Orion's service module performs the translunar injection (TLI) burn.
The TLI burn sends the crew on a path toward the Moon.
On day 5 of Artemis II, Orion enters the moon's sphere of influence.
On day 6 of Artemis II, Orion swings around the far side of the Moon.
On Days 7-10 of Artemis II, the crew travels back to Earth.
Artemis II culminates in a splashdown in the Pacific Ocean around day 10.
On Day 1 of Artemis II, the crew performs a manual flight test of the Orion capsule maneuvering around the spent ICPS upper stage.
The crew will make observations and take photos of the Moon from within 8,000 kilometers (5,000 miles) of the surface.
The Artemis II mission is designed to exceed the 400,000 km distance set by Apollo 13.
The Artemis II mission is the first crewed flight of the Artemis program
